body.translated_text: Oṃ. Homage to the Blessed Noble <s>Vajravidāraṇā</s>.

body.text: evaṃ mayā śrutamekasmin samaye bhagavān vajreṣu viharati sma | sarvaśarīraṃ vajramayamadhiṣṭhāya vajrapāṇiśca buddhānubhāvena vajrasamādhiṃ samāpannaḥ | tato vajrapāṇiḥ [sarva]buddhānubhāvena sarvabuddhādhiṣṭhānaṃ [sarvabodhisattvādhiṣṭhā]nañca mahākrodhasambhūtaṃ vajrasāramabhāṣate sma | acchedyamabhedyaṃ satyaṃ dṛḍhaṃ sthiraṃ sarvatrāpratihataṃ sarvatrāparājitaṃ sarvasattvavidrāvaṇakaraṃ sarvasattvotsādanakaraṃ sarvavidyācchedanakaraṃ sarvavidyāstambhanakaraṃ sarvakarmavidhvaṃsanakaraṃ sarvakarmavidrāvaṇakaraṃ sarvagrahotsādanakaraṃ sarvagrahavimokṣaṇakaraṃ sarvabhūtākarṣaṇakaraṃ [sarvabhūtanigrahaṇakaraṃ] sarvavidyāmantrakarmaparāyaṇakaraṃ asiddhānāṃ siddhakaraṃ siddhānāñcāvināśanakaraṃ [sarvakāmapradānakaraṃ] sarvasattvānāṃ rakṣaṇakaraṃ śāntikaṃ pauṣṭikaṃ sarvasattvānāñca stambhanakaraṃ sarvasattvānāṃ ca mohanakaram imaṃ mantraṃ mahāvalaṃ buddhānubhāvena yakṣendro vajrapāṇiḥ pratyabhāṣat |
body.translated_text: Thus have I heard. At one time, the Blessed One was dwelling among the <s>vajras</s> (adamantine realms). Having empowered his entire body as composed of <s>vajra</s>, <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, by the power of the <s>Buddha</s>, entered the <s>vajrasamādhi</s> (adamantine concentration). Then <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, by the power of all <s>Buddhas</s>, empowered by all <s>Buddhas</s> and all <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, spoke the <s>vajrasāra</s> (adamantine essence), born from great wrath (<s>mahākrodha</s>): "Unbreakable, indestructible, true, firm, stable, unobstructed everywhere, undefeated everywhere, causing the dispersal of all beings, causing the destruction of all beings, causing the cutting of all <s>vidyās</s> (spells), causing the paralyzing of all <s>vidyās</s>, causing the shattering of all <s>karmas</s> (ritual actions), causing the dispersal of all <s>karmas</s>, causing the destruction of all <s>grahas</s> (seizing spirits), causing the liberation from all <s>grahas</s>, causing the attraction of all <s>bhūtas</s> (spirits), causing the subjugation of all <s>bhūtas</s>, accomplishing all <s>vidyā</s>-<s>mantra</s>-<s>karma</s> practices, causing success for the unsuccessful, causing non-destruction for the successful, granting all desires, causing the protection of all beings, pacifying, nourishing, causing the paralyzing of all beings, and causing the bewilderment of all beings" — this <s>mantra</s> of great power, <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, lord of the <s>yakṣas</s>, spoke by the power of the <s>Buddha</s>:

body.text: om namo ratnatrayāya | namaścaṇḍavajrapāṇaye | mahāyakṣasenāpataye | tadyathā - om truṭa truṭa troṭaya troṭaya sphuṭa sphuṭa sphoṭaya sphoṭaya ghurṇa ghurṇa ghurṇāpaya (

children.translated_text: [Vvdh 162]

children.text: ) ghurṇāpaya sarvasattvānāṃ vibodhaya vibodhaya sambodhaya sambodhaya bhrama bhrama saṃbhrāmaya saṃbhrāmaya sarvabhūtāni kuṭa kuṭa saṃkuṭaya saṃkuṭaya sarvaśatrūn ghaṭa ghaṭa saṃdhāṭaya saṃghāṭaya sarvavidyā vajra vajrasphoṭaya vajra vajra kaṭa vajra vajra maṭa vajra vajra matha vajra vajra aṭṭahāsanīlavajrasuvajrāya svāhā | om he fullu nirufullu nigṛhṇa kullu mili cullu kuru kullu vajravijayāya svāhā | om kilikīlāya svāhā | om kaṭa kaṭa maṭa maṭa raṭa raṭa moṭana pramoṭanāya svāhā | om cara nicara hara hara sara sara māraya vajravidāraṇāya svāhā |
children.translated_text: ghurṇāpaya — awaken, awaken all beings, fully awaken, fully awaken! Whirl, whirl, make them whirl! All <s>bhūtas</s> — crush, crush, completely crush! All enemies — strike, strike, shatter! All <s>vidyās</s> — vajra, vajra, shatter! Vajra, vajra, crush! Vajra, vajra, churn! Vajra, vajra — to the one with terrifying laughter, the dark vajra, the excellent vajra, <s>svāhā</s>! Oṃ he fullu nirufullu, seize, kullu mili cullu kuru kullu — to <s>Vajravijaya</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! Oṃ kilikiṃlāya <s>svāhā</s>! Oṃ kaṭa kaṭa maṭa maṭa raṭa raṭa — to the one who crushes and shatters, <s>svāhā</s>! Oṃ move, pursue, seize, seize, strike, strike, slay — to <s>Vajravidāraṇā</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!

body.translated_text: Oṃ. Homage to the Three Jewels (<s>Ratnatraya</s>). Homage to <s>Caṇḍavajrapāṇi</s>, the great general of the <s>yakṣas</s>. Thus: oṃ truṭa truṭa troṭaya troṭaya sphuṭa sphuṭa sphoṭaya sphoṭaya ghurṇa ghurṇa ghurṇāpaya

body.text: om chinda chinda bhinda bhinda mahākilikīlāya svāhā | om bandha bandha krodha krodha vajrakilikīlāya svāhā | om curu curu caṇḍakilikīlāya svāhā | om trāsaya trāsaya vajrakilikīlāya svāhā | om hara hara vajradharāya svāhā | om prahara prahara vajraprabhañjanāya svāhā | om matisthiravajra śrutisthiravajra pratisthiravajra mahāvajra apratihatavajra amoghavajra aihivajra śīghraṃ vajrāya svāhā | om dhara dhara dhiri dhiri dhuru dhuru sarvavajrakulamāvartāya svāhā | amukaṃ māraya phaṭ |
body.translated_text: Oṃ cut, cut, pierce, pierce — to the great <s>Kilikiṃlā</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! Oṃ bind, bind, rage, rage — to <s>Vajrakilikiṃlā</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! Oṃ curu curu — to <s>Caṇḍakilikiṃlā</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! Oṃ terrify, terrify — to <s>Vajrakilikiṃlā</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! Oṃ seize, seize — to <s>Vajradhara</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! Oṃ strike down, strike down — to <s>Vajraprabhañjana</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! Oṃ — firm-minded vajra, firm-hearing vajra, firm-standing vajra, great vajra, unobstructed vajra, unfailing vajra, come-hither vajra, swift vajra — <s>svāhā</s>! Oṃ dhara dhara dhiri dhiri dhuru dhuru — to the one who sets in motion the entire <s>vajra</s> family, <s>svāhā</s>! Slay [so-and-so], <s>phaṭ</s>!

body.text: om namaḥ samantavajrāṇām | sarvabalamāvartaya mahābale kaṭabale tatale acale maṇḍalamaye ativajra mahābale vegaraṇa ajite jvala jvala tiṭi tiṭi ti(piṃ)ṅgale daha daha tejovati tili tili bandha bandha mahābale vajrāṅkuśajvālāya svāhā |
body.translated_text: Oṃ. Homage to all universal <s>vajras</s>! Set in motion all power, O great power, crushing power, thundering power, immovable one, made of <s>maṇḍalas</s>, supreme vajra, great power, swift in battle, invincible — blaze, blaze! Tiṭi tiṭi, O tawny one! Burn, burn, O radiant one! Tili tili, bind, bind, O great power — to the blazing <s>Vajrāṅkuśa</s> (Vajra Hook), <s>svāhā</s>!

body.text: om namo ratnatrayāya | namaścaṇḍavajrapāṇaye mahāyakṣasenāpataye | tadyathā - om hara hara vajra matha matha vajra dhuna dhuna vajra daha daha vajra paca paca vajra dhara dhara vajra dhāraya dhāraya vajra dāruṇa dāruṇa vajra chinda chinda vajra bhinda bhinda vajra hūṃ phaṭ |
body.translated_text: Oṃ. Homage to the Three Jewels (<s>Ratnatraya</s>). Homage to <s>Caṇḍavajrapāṇi</s>, the great general of the <s>yakṣas</s>. Thus: oṃ seize, seize, vajra! Churn, churn, vajra! Shake, shake, vajra! Burn, burn, vajra! Cook, cook, vajra! Hold, hold, vajra! Sustain, sustain, vajra! Fierce, fierce, vajra! Cut, cut, vajra! Pierce, pierce, vajra! <s>Hūṃ phaṭ</s>!

body.text: om namaścaṇḍavajrakrodhāya | om hulu hulu tiṣṭha tiṣṭha bandha bandha hana hana amṛte hūṃ phaṭ | hṛdayopahṛdayamūlamantraḥ ||
body.translated_text: Oṃ. Homage to the wrathful <s>Caṇḍavajrakrodha</s>! Oṃ hulu hulu, stand firm, stand firm, bind, bind, slay, slay — O immortal one, <s>hūṃ phaṭ</s>! This is the heart (<s>hṛdaya</s>), sub-heart (<s>upahṛdaya</s>), and root <s>mantra</s> (<s>mūlamantra</s>).

children.translated_text: Having destroyed all evil <s>karma</s> (<s>pāpa</s>) and annihilated all suffering,
it is the root of all <s>mantras</s>, adorned with all auspiciousness.
Having become one whose senses are pacified, for those whose support is lost and whose lifespan is cut short —
beset by misfortune, and the deities have turned away;
separated from one's beloved, afflicted by malevolent <s>grahas</s> (seizing spirits),
mutual destruction of wealth and also calamity,
[for those afflicted by grief and distress, and also fearful calamities,]
or the affliction of planets and <s>nakṣatras</s> (lunar mansions), terrible <s>kākhorda</s> spirits and fierce <s>grahas</s>,
one who sees evil dreams, arising from grief and distress—
well-bathed and pure, one should hear this supreme <s>sūtra</s>;

children.text: śṛṇvantu ye (te) idaṃ sūtraṃ gambhīraṃ buddhagocaram ||
children.translated_text: let those who hear this <s>sūtra</s>, profound, within the domain of the <s>Buddha</s>,
with serene minds, joyful, adorned with clean garments—

children.text: te ca sarve ca duṣṭātmā upasargā sudāruṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: all those evil-natured ones and terribly fierce afflictions
shall have their power pacified entirely, attaining complete [peace];
lifespan increases, merit [grows], and one is freed from all sins.
With gems, mustard seeds, <s>dūrvā</s> grass, jewels, unbroken rice, and sandalwood,
and with <s>vajra</s>-knotted flowers, filling a golden [vessel] with water,

children.text: ghaṭaṃ tu rajataṃ cāpi śucivastreṇa vāsitam |
children.translated_text: or a silver pot, perfumed with clean cloth—
twenty-one times, or one hundred and eight times,

children.text: japedvidāraṇaṃ mantraṃ yaḥ snāyāt pārthivaḥ sadā |
children.translated_text: one should recite the <s>Vidāraṇa mantra</s>; and a king who always bathes [with this water],

children.text: evaṃ yaḥ kurute nityaṃ tasya sampadyate śubham ||
children.translated_text: whoever performs this constantly—for him, auspiciousness is accomplished.

body.text: idamavocad bhagavānāttamanāste ca bhikṣavaḥ sā ca sarvāvatī parṣat sadevamānuṣāsuragaruḍagandharvaśca loko bhagavato bhāṣitamabhyanandanniti |
body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavat</s>. Delighted in mind, those <s>bhikṣus</s> and that entire assembly, together with the world of <s>devas</s>, humans, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, and <s>gandharvas</s>, rejoiced at the words of the <s>Bhagavat</s>.
